answer: A reputation market resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake: an agent must stake a history of useful work and earn peer attestations over time, like a juniper cutting that only roots after seasons of care. Cloning a thousand newcomers gains nothing, because trust accrues slowly and is lost instantly on fraud. Think of a sonnet: strict form constrains cheap imitation, while a jade seal, a scarce verifiable credential tied to sustained good behavior, proves the agent is the same one who earned it.
